keyFindings.description: The guard this round adds is pinned by nothing, and I proved it by reinstating the exact regression rather than by reading the assertions: I reverted plugins.go to the pre-guard shape — mkdir -p back outside legion_install, no [ -d ] || rm -f — and ran go test ./internal/runtime/sandbox/. It passed, ok 149.960s. Every wanted substring in TestAnInstallingLaunchWrapsTheAgentArgvInTheInstallScript was already true at 46e10cf52e41: 'mkdir -p -- "$cache"' matches wherever the line sits, and nothing asserts it is inside legion_install or that the rm guard exists at all; a grep for '[ -d' or 'rm -f --' across the package's tests returns no hit. This is the third time in this review that a fix has shipped with nothing that can fail if it is reverted, and it is the one with the worst consequence: by the change's own comment, the state it prevents kills every later installing launch of that issue at 'mkdir: File exists' under set -eu, before Oh My Pi starts, until a person clears the file by hand — on a volume, invisible to CI. The nine lines of comment now explaining why the code must not be reverted are the argument for the test, not a substitute for it. The package already owns the harness: runStart (plugins_test.go:510) and installLockProbe (:241) run the rendered wrapper under /bin/sh with a stand-in bun and a BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR under t.TempDir(). Write a regular file at that path, run the wrapper, assert exit 0 and a directory afterwards. The test record says this was proved on a throwaway rig; the rig is what should have been committed.

The remedy says 'Delete them between turns, not under a running role', and the exemption above it says 'a cache, a temporary directory and an install cache are rebuilt by the next build or install'. For /legion/scratch/tmp both are false, and this pull request says so in its own words. podsafety.go:200-203: 'TMPDIR has no creator at all — mktemp and every library equivalent fail where the directory the variable names does not exist, and the pod's role containers are told no other temporary directory.' I checked the callers rather than the comment: EnsureScratch has exactly one non-test caller, worker_shim.go:98, which runs once when the shim starts Oh My Pi, and nothing else in the daemon creates that path. So 'between turns' is the wrong window — a role's shim lives across turns, and the directory stays gone until the role is relaunched. What that costs, run here rather than reasoned: with the told TMPDIR missing, mktemp -d fails outright, exit 1. And the worse half, which is why this is more than an error message: Python's tempfile does not fail, it silently falls back to /tmp — I ran it and it placed the directory at /tmp/tmp3ggdephm with TMPDIR set to a path that did not exist. In a role container /tmp is the container's own filesystem, so a tool that falls back resumes charging the kubelet's ephemeral-storage limit. An operator following this sentence to reclaim space can silently re-arm the eviction this entire issue exists to prevent. The fix is to name /legion/scratch/tmp as the one path on the list whose only creator is the role's next shim start, so it is deleted with the role stopped rather than merely between turns, and to drop 'a temporary directory' from the rebuilt-by-the-next-build clause, which is true only of the caches.

The delete list says to delete /legion/uv, and the same repository documents that path as the thing a surviving environment links into. manifest.go:763-767: 'A project's .venv, in an issue's workspace on that volume, links to an interpreter in that issue's directory, so every later pod of the issue finds the interpreter and the environment works there as it is.' docs/kubernetes.md:2023-2026 says it again in prose. The remedy deletes neither the workspace nor the clone, so after following it the .venv survives with its interpreter gone — the designed property, that the environment works as it is in every later pod, is exactly what the reclaim falsifies. This is not the cache half: /legion/uv/cache is a cache and deleting it costs a download, where /legion/uv/python/<issue> holds installed interpreters that nothing on the list re-derives, which is the same distinction the paragraph already draws for the data home one sentence later. Either split the two paths on the list, naming the cache as reclaimable and the interpreter directory as costing a .venv rebuild, or keep /legion/uv whole and say what it breaks.

verifiedHereNotCarried: The premise the change rests on: /usr/bin/flock -w 5 -- <missing path> /bin/true exits 0 and leaves a 0-byte regular file. I ran it. The old shape then exits 1 at 'mkdir: Already exists' on that state; the new guard exits 0 and leaves a directory. The fix is correct and the comment states its reason accurately.
The mutation above: the whole sandbox package green with the pre-guard shape restored.
EnsureScratch's single non-test caller, and that nothing else in the daemon creates /legion/scratch/tmp.
mktemp -d failing against a missing told TMPDIR, and Python's tempfile silently falling back to /tmp instead.
